title: Introduce Thriftline Policy Compiler and Adaptive Cost Routes
author: Lina Chen
release_notes: Add Thriftline policy compiler: declarative DSL + compiler that emits routing decision graphs and cost-aware quantization profile selectors. Opt-in behind feature flag; rollout via canary cohorts.
description: Motivation: customers need automated levers to translate high-level budget/SLO constraints into runtime routing and quantization choices without manual tuning. This PR introduces the Thriftline Policy Compiler: a small DSL+compiler that synthesizes decision-graph artifacts and associated quant/profile selectors from declarative cost policies. It ships an offline unit-economics simulator used to score candidate policies against historical traces so the compiler chooses the best trade-offs. Implementation summary: added a DSL parser and IR (thriftline/compiler/*); implemented a simulator (thriftline/simulator/simulate.go) that replays trace segments and produces cost/latency distributions; compiler emits decision-graph JSON consumed by a router plugin (router/policy_runner.*) which applies rules at request time; added a thin SDK client and policy examples; added CI job thriftline-e2e to validate simulation vs. small canary traces. Commit summary: feat(dsl): add parser and basic IR; feat(sim): build offline simulator and cost model; feat(emit): decision-graph emitter and JSON schema; feat(router): runtime plugin to evaluate decision graphs; perf(tests): deterministic tie-breaker for routing; test(ci): add thriftline-e2e job and unit tests; docs: thriftline README and rollout notes. Files touched: thriftline/compiler/parser.py, thriftline/compiler/ir.py, thriftline/simulator/simulate.go, router/policy_runner.cc/h, configs/thriftline/default_policies.yaml, tests/thriftline/test_compiler.py, docs/thriftline.md, observability/dashboards/thriftline-overview.json, migrations/20241112_add_thriftline_tags.sql, examples/cost-policies/sample_policy.yaml. Tests and CI: initial e2e failed on a non-deterministic timing assertion; fixed by adding deterministic tie-breaker and test harness time-mocking; final CI passed (all unit and e2e). Review convo highlights: Diego Ramos: "IR looks good but can we collapse conditional node kinds to simplify the runtime?" Author reply: "Collapsed two node kinds into a single comparator node and added deterministic tie-breaker; showed before/after perf numbers in comment." Priya Nair: "Please add telemetry tags that clearly indicate policy id and decision path for postmortems." Author: "Added instrumentation and a migration script to backfill tags; annotated dashboards." Alexei Petrov: "Guardrails around quant selection?" Author: "Runtime will reject compile-time profiles that exceed per-tenant latency budgets; failing profiles are marked and compiler falls back to safer profiles." Approvals: Diego Ramos approved 2024-11-14; Priya Nair approved 2024-11-14; Alexei Petrov approved 2024-11-15. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime flag 'thriftline.enabled'; staged rollout starting with internal canary tenants (1%->10%->50%); competing routes observed in canary and monitoring dashboards added to observability; fallback is fail-open to previous routing. Migration: SQL migration adds thriftline tags for historical telemetry and a one-time backfill job. Impact: non-breaking at API level; runtime gains a small opt-in dependency for decision-graph evaluation. Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2024-11-15. Related work: linear ENG-1358 ENG-1364. Additional notes: included sample policies and a quickstart in docs; performance note: decision-graph evaluation adds ~0.4ms median p99 tail trimmed by caching when policy is stable.
